description:
Advances: ancora.derive
Ready-for: implement
Severity: High (calibrated; pre-existing, exposed by the 2026-09-05 critical review audit of ancora-gg8.9).

Symptom: a lib file containing defmodule Outer do defmodule __MODULE__.Inner do def value, do: :ok end end makes Ancora.Derive.DefIndex raise (literal_segments admits the __MODULE__ tuple and add_definition joins it, Protocol.UndefinedError).
Evidence: before ancora-gg8.9 this crashed mix spec.check with a raw EXIT; since gg8.9 the def_index worker rescue turns it into an env-tier verdict, and the spec_check_test "a nested __MODULE__ name emits a def_index environment verdict" depends on this shape raising (comment at that test).
Why now: valid Elixir fails the gate at the environment tier. Fix DefIndex to resolve __MODULE__ in nested module names (or skip such definitions deterministically), then replace that test fixture with another worker-raising shape.

## Investigation contract, 2026-09-07

Evidence and corrections:
Report: /Users/mz/Documents/my-vault/LLMs/investigations/ancora/2026-09-07-agent-adoption-friction/04-report.md
Measurements: /Users/mz/Documents/my-vault/LLMs/investigations/ancora/2026-09-07-agent-adoption-friction/03-measurements.md
Source revision: 82c2ca8329e1303ececc610dfc9f72986b96c84a. This contract proposes work; no implementation is claimed.

Deliverable:
Resolve a leading __MODULE__ segment against the current lexical module in DefIndex and ModuleLocator, then audit Extract and Resolver for identical names. Support deeper nesting and aliases without repeating the parent prefix. Do not skip valid modules. Replace the existing worker-failure test that depends on this valid syntax failing with an intentional failure injection at the worker boundary.

Verification:
- The saved nested module fixture yields both Outer and Outer.Inner in module membership and includes Inner.value/0 in DefIndex without raising.
- A tagged call to Outer.Inner.value/0 followed by a body change produces the configured drift finding in a disposable git fixture.
- Cover nested __MODULE__ chains, ordinary relative and absolute module names, and lexical scope restoration. The intentional worker failure still produces an environment verdict.
- Cadence: focused tests during implementation; at final verification run mix compile --warnings-as-errors, mix test, mix format --check-formatted, mix deps.unlock --check-unused and mix spec.check against the actual integration base. CI must pass both configured Elixir/OTP combinations. Record evidence of the described symptom after the consuming release before claiming it done.

Allowed touches:
lib/ancora/derive/{def_index,module_locator,extract,resolver}.ex, related tests, ancora.derive spec and relevant decisions.

Out of Scope (files):
Unrelated production modules, credentials, dependencies and consumer repositories. Release metadata belongs to release preparation.

Out of Scope (intent):
No target compilation, broad rescue or silently skipped valid definition.

Merge gate:
- [ ] Focused negative and positive behavior fixtures pass.
- [ ] Affected specs and decisions describe the actual changed behavior.
- [ ] Full repository CI and spec gate pass without cosmetic acknowledgment edits.

Decision:
Resolve valid lexical names. The measured crash and missing locator entry show that rescuing or skipping fixes only the visible failure while losing drift detection.

Open Questions:
None. Unmeasured consumer replay and release behavior are explicit Verification obligations, not claimed results.
title: DefIndex crashes on defmodule __MODULE__.Inner (valid nested module name)
